title: Text of PM’s Departure Statement ahead of visit to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyz Republic
body_text:
I am embarking on a visit to the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from 29 August-1 September 2026.
At the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, I will visit Tashkent on 29-30 August for a State Visit. In recent years, India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership has seen significant advancement. I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan. I will also visit the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, a tribute to the close cultural and people-to-people ties that bind our two countries.
From Tashkent, at the invitation of the President of the Kyrgyz Republic, H.E. Mr. Sadyr Zhaparov, I will travel to Bishkek to participate in the 26th SCO Summit, marking 25 years of this important organisation. India has been an active and constructive member of the SCO since 2017. I look forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, anchored in Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in our neighbourhood and beyond.
I also look forward to meeting President Zhaparov and other SCO leaders, and to attend the Opening Ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games, a celebration of the rich living heritage of Central Asia that India holds in deep respect.
I am confident that this visit will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen our civilisational connect with the region, and advance our shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity, values that lie at the heart of India’s engagement with the world.
****
MJPS/SS/ST

enrichment.summary: Prime Minister Modi is undertaking a visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from 29 August to 1 September 2026. In Tashkent, he will hold a State Visit with President Mirziyoyev to deepen the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership and visit cultural landmarks. He will then travel to Bishkek to attend the 26th SCO Summit, marking 25 years of the organisation, and the Opening Ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.
enrichment.context:
India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in 2017, alongside Pakistan, joining founding members China, Russia, and Central Asian states. The SCO Summit is a key platform for India to engage with Central Asia and Eurasia on security, connectivity, and economic cooperation, and India has repeatedly used it to raise concerns about cross-border terrorism. India's 'Connect Central Asia' policy and the India-Central Asia Summit format reflect New Delhi's strategic interest in the region for energy security, countering Chinese and Pakistani influence, and access via routes like Chabahar port and the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).

The visit to Uzbekistan builds on India's growing strategic partnership with the country, covering defence, trade, and connectivity. Cultural diplomacy elements, such as the Shastri Memorial and Mahatma Gandhi Centre, underscore historical people-to-people ties. India's participation in the World Nomad Games and the emphasis on 'Security, Connectivity and Opportunity' reflect its broader Central Asia policy aimed at countering extremism and expanding regional cooperation amid competing influences from China's Belt and Road Initiative.

prelims_questions.question: India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in which year?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states India has been an active and constructive member of the SCO since 2017.

prelims_questions.question: The 26th SCO Summit mentioned in the PM's departure statement was held in which city?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the PM traveled to Bishkek, the capital of the Kyrgyz Republic, to attend the 26th SCO Summit.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) for India's strategic interests in Central Asia and Eurasia.
Examine India's evolving engagement with Central Asian countries in the context of connectivity, energy security, and counter-terrorism cooperation.

study_notes.reason: The release provides testable facts about SCO membership and India's Central Asia diplomacy while also offering analytical material on India's regional strategic priorities (security, connectivity, opportunity) amid great power competition.

prelims.point: India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in 2017.
prelims.why_important: SCO membership year and India's status (full member since 2017, alongside Pakistan) is a frequently tested fact about India's multilateral engagements.

prelims.point: The 26th SCO Summit (2026) is being held in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, marking 25 years of the organisation's founding.
prelims.why_important: Summit venue, host country and anniversary milestones are typical factual pegs for current affairs-based prelims questions.

prelims.point: The World Nomad Games is a periodic event celebrating Central Asian nomadic/living heritage; the 6th edition's opening ceremony was attended by PM Modi in Kyrgyzstan.
prelims.why_important: An unusual cultural-diplomacy event UPSC could use as a distractor or factual item linking India-Central Asia cultural ties.

prelims.point: SCO founding members include China, Russia, and Central Asian states; India and Pakistan joined as full members together in 2017.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing founding members from later entrants (India, Pakistan) is a classic UPSC comparison-based question format.

mains.point: India's SCO engagement is anchored in the framework of 'Security, Connectivity and Opportunity', reflecting its strategic vision for Central Asia and Eurasia.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers on India's strategic objectives in Eurasia via multilateral platforms like SCO, and how India balances counter-terrorism cooperation with regional connectivity goals.

mains.point: India repeatedly uses SCO platforms to raise concerns about cross-border terrorism, separatism and extremism affecting regional peace and stability.
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on India's approach to combating terrorism through multilateral forums, especially given friction with Pakistan within SCO.

mains.point: India's Central Asia engagement (via SCO, Connect Central Asia policy, India-Central Asia Summit) is partly aimed at countering growing Chinese influence through the Belt and Road Initiative and Pakistani influence in the region.
mains.analytical_use: Helps analyse India's strategic calculus in Central Asia amid great-power competition, useful for 'Discuss India's interests in Central Asia' type questions.

mains.point: India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership spans trade, digital connectivity, defence and energy cooperation, alongside shared development visions (Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan).
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on India's bilateral engagement models with Central Asian states beyond multilateral forums like SCO.

mains.point: India emphasises civilisational and cultural diplomacy (e.g., Shastri Memorial, Gandhi Centre) as a soft-power tool to deepen ties with Central Asia.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on India's soft power and cultural diplomacy as instruments of foreign policy in Central Asia.
